newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Chirac says NATO reform can be finished by Madrid.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says NATO reform can be finished by Madrid.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac expressed optimism on Thursday that internal reform of NATO could be completed in time for the alliance's Madrid summit in July, but left open the question of France's return to its military wing.

"I am very optimistic about the Madrid summit," he told a news conference during a visit to Prague. "There is a problem of general reform. I think that is evolving normally and that the reform could be made formal for Madrid."

Paris wants a European officer to take over from an American at the head of NATO's Naples-based Southern Command if it is to return to the military wing, which it quit in 1966, but Washington has refused.

"If NATO reform allows a European to assume responsibility which would allow a European defence identity to be defined, France is disposed to join," Chirac said on the second day of a state visit to the Czech Republic.

"If by contrast, for reasons which I understand perfectly and pose no problems between the United States and France, the Americans plan to keep complete mastery of NATO, France will stay in its present situation," he said.
NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) is set to invite new members to join the alliance after the Madrid summit. The Czechs, Poles and Hungarians are the leading candidates.
